name: GitHub Copilot SDK — built-in tools (shell + files)
summary: Copilot SDK's built-in shell/files/URL tools running against the BYOM APIM route.
description: The GitHub Copilot SDK ships built-in tools that the agent can call: shell command execution, file read/write, and URL fetch. They're opt-in via `on_permission_request` in `SessionConfig` — every use raises a permission request that the host approves or denies. This card verifies those tools still function when the SDK is pointed at our APIM AI Gateway (BYOK topology) rather than the default GitHub-hosted model backend.
notes:
Cannot be probed from GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners because our APIM has `publicNetworkAccess=disabled` — the direct route returns 403 (see `copilot-sdk-via-apim-direct`). Verification path is the `copilot-canary` hosted agent in the `ai-gateway-pe-testing` infra repo: it lives inside the Foundry VNet, auto-approves every `on_permission_request` per the Agent Framework devblog pattern, and runs three sub-probes per invocation — `chat` (plain BYOK ping), `bash` (`echo <sentinel>` via the shell tool, asserts sentinel round-trips through the model), `files` (write/read a randomized payload to a temp file via the files tool, asserts the payload round-trips *and* is present on disk).

Flip this card to `supported` once `azd deploy` on the infra repo publishes `HOSTED_AGENT_NAME_COPILOT_CANARY` and the pytest here shows all three sub-probes green.
